page: Microsoft Azure M96bds_2_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor with an x86_64 architecture, featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs, 48 physical cores, and a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The processor includes a 105 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance is equipped with 1946.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.27 GB of RAM per core, and includes 4608 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in memory bandwidth, with read-only small block, read-only large block, and write large block operations all placing in the top 10%. Multi-threaded operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by top-tier results in bzip3 multi-threaded decompression and PassMark CPU scores, including extended instructions and encryption tests. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the middle 50%. Database operations on PassMark and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 10%, while Redis SET operations and LLM inference speeds for medium and large models consistently place in the top 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets rather than raw single-threaded compute speed. The primary tradeoff is the average single-core performance relative to its top-tier multi-threaded and memory bandwidth capabilities. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching, enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
